questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Crystal Field Splitting CFSE in Ligand Fields
questions.question: The octahedral complex $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ in [Coordination Compounds] exists as cis and trans geometrical isomers. Which of the following statements is strictly correct regarding their optical activity?
options: The cis-isomer is chiral and optically active; the trans-isomer possesses a center of inversion and is optically inactive
Both cis and trans isomers are optically active
Both cis and trans isomers are optically inactive
The trans-isomer is optically active and cis is inactive
questions.solution: The trans-isomer has an inversion center (and mirror plane) and is achiral (optically inactive). The cis-isomer has no plane or center of inversion ($C_2$ symmetry) and exists as a pair of non-superimposable enantiomers (optically active).
questions.explanation: Analyze using fundamental chemical principles in Coordination Compounds.
tags: Crystal Field Splitting CFSE in Ligand Fields

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Crystal Field Splitting CFSE in Ligand Fields
questions.question: What is the spin-only magnetic moment (in Bohr Magnetons, rounded to the nearest integer) of the high-spin complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ in [Coordination Compounds]? (Take $\sqrt{35} \approx 6$)
questions.solution: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ has $d^5$ electron configuration. Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak-field ligand, it forms a high-spin complex with $n = 5$ unpaired electrons. $\mu = \sqrt{5(5 + 2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM} \approx 6$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative laws in Coordination Compounds.
tags: Crystal Field Splitting CFSE in Ligand Fields
